name: decide which of two ordinary notes hides a word
one_line: Two notes that read as notes, and in one of them the first letters of the lines spell something when read downwards.
how: Print two notes of seven lines each, of the sort left on a kitchen table. In one, the initials of the lines spell an Italian word read down the margin; in the other they spell nothing. Ask which of the two it is, what the word is, and then how many letters had to be looked at: fourteen out of the four hundred and thirteen on the page. That last number is the whole point — the cost is not in checking an acrostic but in thinking to check one. Close with the fact: in Modena in 1859 people wrote Viva V.E.R.D.I. on walls, and whoever passed read the name of a composer.

knobs.knob: which letter of the line is read
knobs.effect: First and last are positions that exist without being declared, so the form announces itself. A letter in the middle is not a position at all and has to be marked with a capital or a column, or nobody finds it.

knobs.knob: whether the lines are written or found
knobs.effect: Written, the surface has to carry a constraint and most drafts read as forced. Found — open a book, take the first line holding the letter you need — the constraint stays and the writing cost goes.

knobs.knob: how visible it is meant to be
knobs.effect: A capital or a wider margin makes it a signature that anybody sees. Nothing at all makes it a hiding place, and then it depends entirely on somebody suspecting there is anything there.
A note that only makes sense once the hidden word is found is a failed one, because the column was all there was. A note that reads as a note and also hides something pays twice.

where_the_work_is: In the second note, the one that hides nothing. It has to look exactly as deliberate as the first, or the question answers itself before anybody has read a line of either.
breaks: The initials have to line up, so a ragged left edge destroys it; set both notes flush left. Scanned back it reads. On 800x480 half a note fits, though four short lines are exactly a four-letter acrostic and that is worth trying. Nothing here needs a letter counted inside a word, since a first letter is a first letter, so this is the one form in its chapter that composes without a hand check.
